gate-is-in-process-and-cannot-fail: The TS marker writers asked Rust over the rustInvoke channel store_version_gate before every write, and the goldens record those calls (gateCalls) and, for the three cases that script a rejected channel, the warning 'bottle version gate: Rust could not be asked'. The Rust crate calls gamelib_store::version_gate in process, so there is no channel to reject and no such warning; the replay compares neither the recorded channel calls nor that one warning line. The three gate cases (reconcile-gate-rejected, record-pinned-gate-rejected, record-crossover-gate-rejected) and record-pinned-gate-answers-newer still replay: the test injects a gate that cannot be asked, or that answers newer, through the writers' Gate parameter, and the refusal (nothing written, false or null returned) is compared byte for byte.
unreadable-marker-is-rewritten-as-the-ts: 87-11 finding 8: reconcile and recordPinnedBottleEngine overwrite a marker whose bytes are not a JSON object (the gate reports 'unreadable', which is writable), and only a marker a newer build wrote (version above 1) is never touched. The port keeps that, because the goldens (record-pinned-over-unreadable-overwritten, reconcile-marker-unreadable) record it and D-07 asks for the same bytes on disk. A marker that is unreadable is derived state with nothing recoverable in it, and the reconcile pass is what repairs it before a CrossOver probe adds a Timestamp. The round trip (roundtrip_state.rs) never rewrites an unreadable marker blindly: read returns nothing for it, so there is nothing to write back, and its bytes stay identical.
